Convex Functions

This scene studies functions whose chords float above the graph. Convexity turns out to be the derivative increasing.

Picture a bowl shape opening upward. A curve whose slope keeps growing is convex. The middle height never exceeds the average of the end heights.

For example, stretch a 🧵 string taut between two points on a bowl-shaped curve and it always floats above the curve. The string's middle sits higher than the curve's middle.

Prove directly that f(x)=x2f(x) = x^2f(x)=x2 is convex.

(tx+(1−t)y)2≤tx2+(1−t)y2  ⟺  t(1−t)(x−y)2≥0(tx+(1-t)y)^2 \le tx^2+(1-t)y^2 \iff t(1-t)(x-y)^2 \ge 0(tx+(1−t)y)2≤tx2+(1−t)y2⟺t(1−t)(x−y)2≥0
Show proof

  1. Expanding the difference gives tx2+(1−t)y2−(tx+(1−t)y)2=t(1−t)(x−y)2tx^2+(1-t)y^2-(tx+(1-t)y)^2 = t(1-t)(x-y)^2tx2+(1−t)y2−(tx+(1−t)y)2=t(1−t)(x−y)2. (Squaring (tx+(1−t)y)(tx+(1-t)y)(tx+(1−t)y) and collecting terms factors t(1−t)t(1-t)t(1−t) out of the x2x^2x2 and y2y^2y2 coefficients.)

  2. Since t∈[0,1]t \in [0,1]t∈[0,1], we have t(1−t)≥0t(1-t) \ge 0t(1−t)≥0, and (x−y)2≥0(x-y)^2 \ge 0(x−y)2≥0 as a square. So the right-hand side is nonnegative.

  3. That is, (tx+(1−t)y)2≤tx2+(1−t)y2(tx+(1-t)y)^2 \le tx^2+(1-t)y^2(tx+(1−t)y)2≤tx2+(1−t)y2 — the definition of convexity holds, so x2x^2x2 is convex. This is also why the max gap is 111 for a=−1,b=1a=-1, b=1a=−1,b=1 in the picture above.

log⁡a+b2≥log⁡a+log⁡b2=log⁡ab\log\frac{a+b}{2} \ge \frac{\log a + \log b}{2} = \log\sqrt{ab}log2a+b​≥2loga+logb​=logab​
